title: Fewshot Surgeon: Tinkering Log
summary: Ad-hoc lab notes for iterating small curated few-shot sets and surgical template edits; focused on brittle examples, anchor choice, and token-budget heuristics.
body:
Purpose:
Quick, portable log for 'surgical' few-shot edits — slice in/out exemplars, swap anchors, probe failure modes. Not a canonical repo artifact (yet) — intended for rapid hypothesis capture and handoff to Lina/Marco for evals.

High-level goals (what I'm trying to learn):
- Which single-exemplar swap produces largest shift in model output distribution for a given instruction pattern (esp. role-anchored prompts).
- Understand when exemplar-ordering beats exemplar-content for few-shot style signals.
- Cheap heuristics to prune exemplars under strict token budgets without degrading accuracy more than ~2-3%.

Quick experiment log (chronological):
- 2024-11-08: Baseline set A (5 exemplars) for 'extractive summary' task. Observed high variance on numeric extraction when exemplar numbers vary in magnitude.
- 2024-11-15: Performed single-exemplar swap with an extreme numeric case (1e9) -> output collapsed to text-only summary, model omitted small numbers. Hypothesis: numeric magnitude in exemplar anchors numeric formatting preference.
- 2024-11-20: Tried reordering exemplars by 'presentation clarity' (short -> long). Ordering reduced hallucinated fields in 60% of trials, but increased token length of outputs.
- 2024-11-27: Token-budget pruning: greedy remove exemplar with lowest mutual information proxy (simple lexical overlap metric). Retained performance within 1.8% on accuracy but lost some diversity.

Surgical templates (working drafts):
- Template T1 (role-anchored, explicit format):
  "You are an expert data summarizer. Given input document, extract these fields:
   - title
   - key_metrics (number + unit)
   - 1-sentence summary
  Provide output as JSON with keys: title, key_metrics, summary."

- Template T2 (contrastive exemplar cueing):
  "Below are examples of inputs -> JSON outputs. Use them to follow the same pattern for the new input. Mark uncertain fields as null.

  EX1:
  [input text]
  -> { ... }

  EX2:
  [input text]
  -> { ... }

  NEW:
  [new input]
  ->"

Notes on exemplar selection heuristics (practical):
- Anchor diversity matters: include 1 short, 1 mid, 1 verbose exemplar when intent is 'formatting + content extraction'.
- Avoid two exemplars that share the same rare token (e.g., proprietary product name) — they bias token-level attention and create overfitting.
- If target includes numbers, ensure exemplar set spans the order-of-magnitude range you expect; otherwise model may choose a default numeric pattern.

Observed failure cases (examples + quick repro):
- Failure F1: Inconsistent field typing
  - Prompt: T1 + 3 exemplars (numbers included).
  - Repro: Model returns numbers as words for small values and numerals for large ones.
  - Quick mitigation: in exemplar outputs, normalize number format (always numerals) and add instruction: "Always use digits for numeric values."

- Failure F2: Overfitting to punctuation style
  - Repro: Exemplar outputs use trailing commas in lists; model copies that style into single-item lists -> awkward punctuation.
  - Mitigation: explicit instruction line: "Do not introduce trailing commas; ensure standard JSON formatting."

- Failure F3: Anchor bleed when exemplars contradict each other
  - Repro: Two exemplars show different tag schemas (camelCase vs snake_case). Model randomly mixes both.
  - Mitigation: canonicalize exemplar outputs to target schema; add line: "Use snake_case only."

Mini-experiments to run next (priority ordered):
1) Single-exemplar influence map: for a fixed 5-exemplar set, swap each exemplar with a neutral example (same length but different content) and measure output edit distance distribution. Goal: rank exemplars by influence. (Linear: ML-312)
2) Token-budget pruning ablation: run greedy vs random removal vs MI-proxy removal on 100 inputs; measure accuracy, F1, and formatting errors.
3) Anchor-order ablation: test short->long, long->short, interleaved; measure hallucination rate.

Example few-shot sets (raw, minimal):
- FS-A (task: extract metrics)
  EX1_IN: "Q3 earnings call: revenue grew to $1.2B, up 8% year-over-year. Gross margin 55%."
  EX1_OUT: "{\"title\": \"Q3 earnings call\", \"key_metrics\": \"revenue: 1.2B; growth: 8%\", \"summary\": \"Revenue up 8% YoY, gross margin 55%\" }"
  EX2_IN: "Release notes: deployed feature X, latency dropped from 200ms to 120ms (40% improvement)."
  EX2_OUT: "{\"title\": \"Release notes - feature X\", \"key_metrics\": \"latency: 200ms->120ms (40%)\", \"summary\": \"Latency improved 40% after feature X deployment\" }"

- FS-B (task: instruction-following with conservative fallback)
  EX1_IN: "Classify sentiment and give a one-sentence recommendation."
  EX1_OUT: "{\"sentiment\": \"positive\", \"recommendation\": \"Proceed with broader rollout\" }"
  EX2_IN: "Classify sentiment and give a one-sentence recommendation (if unclear, say 'insufficient data')."
  EX2_OUT: "{\"sentiment\": null, \"recommendation\": \"insufficient data\" }"

Practical notes / debugging heuristics:
- When outputs flip types across runs, toggle temperature to 0 and re-run — if instability persists it's likely exemplar ambiguity not sampling noise.
- Add tiny explicit anchors like: "If value unknown, return null." That single line often reduces ad-hoc guesswork.
- For low-token budgets, prefer fewer exemplars that cover extremes rather than many similar mid-range examples.

Handoff checklist for Lina/Marco (what I want them to run):
- Run influence-map job (see ML-312) on 2 host models: hosted-v1 and dedicated-quantized-v3. Capture exemplar rank delta and percentage of formatting errors.
- Run token-pruning ablation with 500 random inputs from prod-sample-2024 and log cases where formatting/JSON validity fails.
- Capture top 30 failure examples and patch exemplar set; iterate until formatting errors < 2%.

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Can we craft an automatic exemplar-suggester that optimizes for coverage across token n-gram clusters instead of simple lexical overlap? (sketch idea: cluster candidate exemplars by embedding distance, pick centroids)
- Should we add lightweight evals in Console for formatting regressions (JSON validity + schema match) per rollout? low-cost guardrail.

Random quick ideas to try later:
- Swap out last exemplar with 'contradictory' example to intentionally increase model conservatism (useful for safety experiments).
- Use tiny synthetic exemplars that contain negative examples ("wrong format") labelled explicitly, to teach model to avoid that class.

End-of-log.
Notes: keep iterations short, log one concrete numeric metric per run (accuracy, json-valid-rate, token-delta). Share raw test cases in the ML-312 issue thread.
